title: progress.31337.json is written with a hard-coded deploymentStatus "completed" during forge's local-execution phase, before any transaction is broadcast
propagation: PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET (as a pattern — this shape has already poisoned three committed mainnet progress files)
description: `_writeProgressFile()` emits `"deploymentStatus": "completed"` as a string LITERAL (:1922), derived from nothing, and is called after `vm.stopBroadcast()` — i.e. during forge's local execution pass, before the broadcast begins. The file also hard-codes `"chainId": 31337` (:1919) rather than reading `block.chainid`, and hard-codes its own output path (:1943). It contains no timestamp and no deployer field, so a stale file is byte-indistinguishable from a fresh one.
impact: Benign in isolation on anvil — DeployMocks never reads a progress file (no vm.readFile/parseJson anywhere) and clean:local deletes it first, so there is no resume consumer to mislead. It is NOT benign as a pattern: package.json's `//uniboost-cutover:resume` doc comment records this exact shape already producing three committed `progress.uniboost-cutover.1.POISONED*.bak` files on mainnet, where a crashed broadcast left a file positively asserting completion. Combined with the total absence of a chain-id guard (DEV-05), a mis-pointed RPC would produce a progress file that positively asserts it is anvil output.
attackPath: No attack path. _writeProgressFile emits `"deploymentStatus": "completed"` as a string LITERAL (:1922) derived from nothing, and runs during forge's local execution pass after vm.stopBroadcast() - i.e. before the broadcast has actually landed.
evidence: Empirically confirmed during this audit: progress.31337.json mtime 2026-07-29 12:14:24 while the broadcast was still in flight at 12:17:45 (deployer nonce 160 of 352). The file claimed 'completed' for a further ~15 minutes of unconfirmed broadcasting. Separately, a cold redeploy reproduced the committed file BYTE-IDENTICALLY (md5 f4bb1d9f42d24416dd8a4622ab6b21c7), which is a positive determinism result but also means no field distinguishes a fresh file from a stale one.
recommendation: For the mainnet port, do not inherit this. Use `DeployMainnetUniboostBatchMinters.s.sol:214`'s `_isDeployed` (which additionally requires `a.code.length > 0`) as the source of truth for resume, and treat the progress file as advisory. Locally, at minimum read `block.chainid` rather than hard-coding 31337, and add a timestamp so staleness is detectable.

severityRationale: LOW, matching the auditor's proposal. Not raised to Medium despite the corroborating evidence that this exact shape has already produced three committed progress.uniboost-cutover.1.POISONED*.bak files on mainnet: that damage is the recorded consequence on OTHER entry points and is not re-charged here, and on the dev entry point there is demonstrably no consumer. A poisoned progress file misleads a human but does not itself impair protocol function or put an asset at risk, and a correct source of truth already exists in-repo (DeployMainnetUniboostBatchMinters.s.sol:214 `_isDeployed`, which additionally requires `a.code.length > 0`). Not dropped to QA either: the hard-coded `"chainId": 31337` (:1919) combined with DEV-05's total absence of a chain-id guard means a mis-pointed RPC would produce a file positively asserting it is anvil output, and the file carries no timestamp and no deployer, so a stale file is byte-indistinguishable from a fresh one (independently confirmed - a cold redeploy reproduced it byte-identically, md5 f4bb1d9f42d24416dd8a4622ab6b21c7). That is a real state-handling defect worth a Low.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
